body: Colony Wars: Vengeance is Psygnosis's PlayStation space-combat game, first released in North America on 3 November 1998. The sequel follows Mertens, a pilot in the Colonial Navy, changing sides from the viewpoint established by the original. Missions place the player in starfighters equipped for particular tasks, with results affecting the route through the campaign. Victory and defeat therefore do more than end an individual sortie. They help determine which part of the larger conflict the player encounters next, giving the pilot's performance consequences beyond a score or a completed objective.

Different starfighters carry combinations of energy weapons, missiles and torpedoes, while some tasks require nonlethal EMP attacks or a grapple to capture an important target. Countermeasures offer a response to incoming missiles. The player must identify what the mission asks for and use the available systems accordingly, rather than treating every object in space as something to destroy. Collected power pods improve attributes such as manoeuvrability and shield capacity. Those upgrades connect completed sorties to the handling of the next one, giving progress a practical effect within the cockpit.

Vengeance adds missions inside planetary atmospheres, widening the series beyond its original space engagements. The campaign also introduces large League machines known as Sentinels, giving the pilot another scale of opponent to confront. Stephen Murphy composed the score for a story still organised around the consequences of success and failure. European release followed later in November 1998. Its most important change is the viewpoint itself: a continuing fictional war becomes less settled when the player takes the controls of a pilot serving the force that previously stood on the other side.
